record.paper_title: Exchange Bias and Interface-related Effects in Two-dimensional van der Waals Magnetic Heterostructures: Open Questions and Perspectives
record.original_question: Can ferromagnet/ferromagnet coupling at a defective van der Waals VSe2/MoS2 interface generate an exchange-bias effect even though the interface is not a conventional ferromagnet/antiferromagnet interface?

evidence.quote: The large enhancement of MS and HC in MoS2/VSe2 (Fig. 9b) due to the exchange interaction between the VSe2 and MoS2 layers raises an important question: Can this FM/FM interaction lead to an exchange bias effect?
Kalappattil et al. recently observed a sizable EB effect in the monolayer VSe2/single crystal MoS2 heterostructure (see Fig. 9b,c), which is absent in the case of the VSe2/HOPG system [64].

artifact.category_tag: Exchange bias in van der Waals magnetic heterostructures
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a van der Waals heterostructure formed by a monolayer of VSe2 (a transition-metal dichalcogenide that, in monolayer form, exhibits ferromagnetic ordering attributed to defects and edge states) deposited on a single crystal of MoS2 (another transition-metal dichalcogenide whose pristine bulk form is nonmagnetic but which, with defects, can host localized magnetic moments behaving as a weak ferromagnet). In conventional exchange-bias (EB) systems, a horizontal shift of the magnetic hysteresis loop along the applied-field axis arises at an interface between a ferromagnet (FM) and an antiferromagnet (AFM) after field cooling, due to unidirectional anisotropy imprinted by the pinned AFM moments on the FM. The VSe2/MoS2 interface, however, is nominally an FM/FM interface (both layers being defect-induced ferromagnets) rather than an FM/AFM interface.

Question: Can the interfacial exchange coupling between two defect-induced ferromagnets at a van der Waals VSe2/MoS2 interface produce a genuine exchange-bias effect (i.e., a measurable horizontal shift of the field-cooled hysteresis loop), despite the absence of a conventional antiferromagnetic pinning layer? Equivalently, determine whether FM/FM coupling at such a defective vdW interface is a viable mechanism for exchange bias, and if so characterize the conditions (defect density, interfacial coupling strength, anisotropy, temperature) under which a finite EB field is expected.
artifact.status_search_result: Experimental work by Kalappattil et al. reported a sizable exchange-bias effect in a monolayer VSe2/single-crystal MoS2 heterostructure (absent in VSe2/HOPG), indicating that an FM/FM-type interface in this defective vdW system does yield an EB signal. The microscopic mechanism—how FM/FM coupling at a defective vdW interface produces unidirectional anisotropy—remains under active investigation, so the underlying theoretical question is only partially resolved.

status_evidence.title: Exchange bias and interface-related effects in two-dimensional van der Waals magnetic heterostructures
status_evidence.snippet: Exchange bias effects have been reported in bilayers composed of different van der Waals magnetic materials, including VSe2/MoS2 heterostructures, described as bilayers of two different van der Waals defective magnets.
status_evidence.claim: A sizable EB effect was observed in monolayer VSe2/MoS2 although the interface is FM/FM rather than FM/AFM, supporting the affirmative answer.

status_evidence.title: Strong room-temperature ferromagnetism in VSe2 monolayers on vdW substrates
status_evidence.snippet: Single-layer VSe2 grown by MBE shows enhanced magnetic moment and ferromagnetic ordering robust above room temperature.
status_evidence.claim: Monolayer VSe2 is ferromagnetic, so the VSe2/MoS2 interface is FM/FM in nature.
